title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 10 Artificial Intelligence (417) · Crash revision of the theory units (2026-27)
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions written from this video's script, its worksheet and the NCERT/CBSE material it cites, modelled on most-repeated / high-weightage question types in CBSE Sample Question Papers and past board papers. Practice for readiness only: not predictions of any exam and no promise of marks.
instructions: 39 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number. Rough work on paper is fine.

patterns.T3: Stages of the AI Project Cycle
patterns.T12: FP / FN and which metric matters

S1.name: Part A: Employability Skills
S1.tip: Part A is list-based: self-motivation steps (strengths → goals → plan → stay loyal), SMART goals, strong passwords, entrepreneur functions, 17 SDGs. Case questions: name the skill the person shows.
S1.ncert: Employability Skills Class X (Part A) units on communication, self-management, ICT, entrepreneurship and green skills; CBSE SQP 2025-26 Part A

S2.name: AI Project Cycle & Domains
S2.tip: Six stages in order: scope, acquire, explore, model, evaluate, deploy. Domain = type of data: numbers/tables → Statistical Data, images/video → CV, human language → NLP. Always add the one-line reason.
S2.ncert: CBSE AI (417) Facilitator Handbook Class X, Unit 1 (AI Project Cycle, AI domains); CBSE SQP 2025-26 Q11

S3.name: Ethical Frameworks & Bioethics
S3.tip: Sector-based (bioethics in healthcare) vs value-based (rights, utility, virtue). Bioethics is sector-based. For biased-algorithm cases: name the unfair data, then the principle.
S3.ncert: CBSE AI (417) Facilitator Handbook Class X, Unit 1 (ethical frameworks); CBSE SQP 2025-26 Q17

S4.name: Modelling: AI, ML, DL & Learning Types
S4.tip: AI ⊃ ML ⊃ DL. Label output → classification; number output → regression. No labels: clustering (groups) or association (bought X, also bought Y). Reward and penalty → reinforcement.
S4.ncert: CBSE AI (417) Facilitator Handbook Class X, Unit 2 (Advanced Modelling); CBSE AI Curriculum 2026-27 Unit 2

S5.name: Neural Networks
S5.tip: Layers: input → hidden → output. CNN is for images; ANN learns features itself. Perceptron: y = w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + … + b; multiply, add, then add the bias.
S5.ncert: CBSE AI (417) Facilitator Handbook Class X, Unit 2 (neural networks); CBSE SQP 2025-26 Q12

S6.name: Evaluating Models
S6.tip: Draw the confusion matrix first. Accuracy = (TP + TN)/total; Precision = TP/(TP + FP); Recall = TP/(TP + FN); F1 = 2PR/(P + R). Missed cases dangerous → watch recall; false alarms costly → watch precision.
S6.ncert: CBSE AI (417) Facilitator Handbook Class X, Unit 3 (Evaluating Models); CBSE SQP 2025-26 Q20

S7.name: Computer Vision
S7.tip: Pixel = smallest unit; resolution = number of pixels. Byte image: 0 (black) to 255 (white). RGB has 3 channels, grayscale 1. CV is the superset of image processing.
S7.ncert: CBSE AI (417) Facilitator Handbook Class X, Unit 5 (Computer Vision); CBSE SQP 2025-26 Q15

S8.name: Natural Language Processing
S8.tip: Bag of Words: normalise → dictionary → document vector → all vectors; only counts matter. Stem may not be a real word; lemma always is. Script bot = rules; smart bot = coded, big data.
S8.ncert: CBSE AI (417) Facilitator Handbook Class X, Unit 6 (NLP); CBSE SQP 2025-26 Q16, Q21

questions.question: How many Sustainable Development Goals has the United Nations set?
questions.explanation: The UN has 17 SDGs (for example, donating unused things fits SDG 12, responsible consumption).
questions.remediation: Video part 1: Part A: Employability Skills; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: A nod or a thumbs-up is an example of:
questions.explanation: Gestures and body language are non-verbal communication.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: Part A: Employability Skills; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which of these is the strongest password?
questions.explanation: A strong password mixes upper- and lower-case letters, numbers and special characters, and avoids names and simple sequences.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: Part A: Employability Skills; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Meera has listed what she is good at. According to the steps to self-motivation, what should she do next?
questions.explanation: The four steps: find your strengths → set goals → make a plan → stay loyal to your goals.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: Part A: Employability Skills; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Skip planning and start at once
Set goals she wants to achieve
Ask others to plan for her

questions.question: Which is the FIRST stage of the AI Project Cycle?
questions.explanation: Order: problem scoping → data acquisition → data exploration → modelling → evaluation → deployment.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: AI Project Cycle & Domains; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: A team tests its trained model on fresh data it has never seen to check how well it works. This stage is:
questions.explanation: Testing a model on new data is evaluation; deployment is putting it into real use.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: AI Project Cycle & Domains; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Problem scoping uses the 4Ws. They are:
questions.explanation: The 4Ws canvas: Who, What, Where, Why.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: AI Project Cycle & Domains; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: A hospital system reads chest X-ray images and flags possible pneumonia. Which AI domain is this?
questions.explanation: Name the domain from the type of input data: X-ray images → Computer Vision.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: AI Project Cycle & Domains; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Natural Language Processing, because it gives a diagnosis
Statistical Data, because hospitals keep records
Natural Language Processing, because doctors write reports
Computer Vision, because the input is images

questions.question: A water board uses 20 years of rainfall and usage tables to forecast next month's water demand. Choose the domain WITH the correct reason.
questions.explanation: The data is numerical and tabular, so it is Statistical Data; the reason must be built on the data type.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: AI Project Cycle & Domains; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Statistical Data, because it learns from numbers in tables
Computer Vision, because it predicts the future
Computer Vision, because rainfall can be seen
NLP, because the board writes reports on it

questions.question: Bioethics, used in healthcare, is an example of a:
questions.explanation: Bioethics is built for one field (healthcare), so it is sector-based.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: Ethical Frameworks & Bioethics; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: A virtue-based ethical framework mainly looks at:
questions.explanation: Virtue-based = character and intentions; utility-based = maximum benefit; rights-based = rights.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: Ethical Frameworks & Bioethics; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: The rules of one particular sector
The greatest benefit for the greatest number
The character and intentions of the person acting

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: A is false: bioethics is sector-based. R is true, and it is exactly why bioethics is sector-based.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: Ethical Frameworks & Bioethics; then the worksheet practice for this part.
questions.reason: Bioethics is applied in the field of healthcare.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: An AI tool that shortlists patients for a free check-up was trained mostly on records from one city, and it gives poorer results for patients from villages. What is the most likely reason it is unfair?
questions.explanation: Bias usually comes from unrepresentative data; the fix links to principles like 'do not harm' and 'give justice'.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: Ethical Frameworks & Bioethics; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: The model used too few hidden layers
The training data did not represent all groups of patients
The patients typed their names wrongly

questions.question: Which statement about AI, ML and DL is correct?
questions.explanation: Nested circles: AI ⊃ ML ⊃ DL.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Modelling: AI, ML, DL & Learning Types; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: AI is a part of Machine Learning
AI, ML and DL do not overlap
Machine Learning is a part of Deep Learning
Deep Learning is a part of Machine Learning, which is a part of AI

questions.question: A self-parking car learns by getting rewards for good moves and penalties for bad ones. This is:
questions.explanation: Learning by reward and penalty is reinforcement learning.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Modelling: AI, ML, DL & Learning Types; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Predicting tomorrow's maximum temperature in °C is an example of:
questions.explanation: The output is a continuous number, so it is regression.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Modelling: AI, ML, DL & Learning Types; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: A shop groups its customers by buying habits, without any labels given in advance. This is:
questions.explanation: Unlabelled data grouped into similar sets is clustering (unsupervised).
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Modelling: AI, ML, DL & Learning Types; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Why does a rule-based chatbot fail when a user types a new slang word it was never given?
questions.explanation: Rule-based models follow fixed rules, so their learning is static.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Modelling: AI, ML, DL & Learning Types; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Its learning is static: it follows fixed rules and cannot adapt
It has too much training data

questions.question: Which of these tasks is CLASSIFICATION?
questions.explanation: Ask: is the answer a label or a number? Approve / reject is a label; the rest are numbers (regression).
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Modelling: AI, ML, DL & Learning Types; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Deciding whether a loan application should be approved or rejected
Predicting the price of a flat in rupees

questions.question: The three kinds of layers in a neural network are:
questions.explanation: Input layer → one or more hidden layers → output layer.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: Neural Networks; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is mainly used for:
questions.explanation: A CNN assigns weights to image features to tell one object from another.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: Neural Networks; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: A perceptron has inputs x₁ = 2 and x₂ = 3, weights w₁ = 4 and w₂ = −1, and bias b = 5. Find the output y = w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + b.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: Neural Networks; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: A perceptron has inputs (1, 2, 3), weights (2, w₂, −1) and bias 4. Its output is 9. Find w₂.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: Neural Networks; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: In a confusion matrix, a FALSE POSITIVE means the model:
questions.explanation: False positive = a false alarm, like a fire alarm with no fire. A missed real case is a false negative.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: Evaluating Models; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Said 'yes', but the real answer was 'no'
Said 'no', and the real answer was 'no'
Said 'no', but the real answer was 'yes'
Said 'yes', and the real answer was 'yes'

questions.question: A screening model tested on 200 cases gives TP = 30, FP = 10, FN = 30, TN = 130. Find its accuracy as a percentage.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: Evaluating Models; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: For the same model (TP = 30, FP = 10, FN = 30, TN = 130), find the precision as a percentage.
questions.explanation: Precision = TP/(TP + FP) = 30/40 = 0.75 = 75%.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: Evaluating Models; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: For the same model (TP = 30, FP = 10, FN = 30, TN = 130), find the recall as a percentage.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: Evaluating Models; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: For the same model, precision = 0.75 and recall = 0.5. Find the F1 score as a percentage.
questions.explanation: F1 = 2PR/(P + R) = 2 × 0.75 × 0.5 / 1.25 = 0.75/1.25 = 0.6 = 60%. Note how the low recall pulls F1 down even though accuracy is 80%.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: Evaluating Models; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: For a model that screens patients for a serious disease, which metric matters most?
questions.explanation: When missing a real case is dangerous, false negatives matter most, so watch recall. High accuracy can mislead.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: Evaluating Models; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Recall, because missing a real case (false negative) is dangerous
Accuracy, because it is always reliable
Precision, because false alarms are the only problem
None, because metrics do not matter in health

questions.question: Why should a model not be tested on the same data it was trained on?
questions.explanation: Testing on training data hides overfitting and shows fake-high accuracy; use a separate testing set.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: Evaluating Models; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: It always lowers accuracy to zero
It makes the model run faster
It gives a falsely high accuracy because the model has already seen those answers (overfitting)

questions.question: In a byte image, what is the highest possible pixel value (white)?
questions.explanation: 8 bits give 2⁸ = 256 values, from 0 (black) to 255 (white).
questions.remediation: Video part 7: Computer Vision; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: A traffic camera finds and boxes every car and every person in one frame. This Computer Vision task is:
questions.explanation: Classification labels one object; classification + localisation also locates it; object detection finds many objects; instance segmentation marks each one pixel by pixel.
questions.remediation: Video part 7: Computer Vision; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: A tiny RGB image is 4 pixels wide and 4 pixels high. How many numbers (channel values) does the computer store for it?
questions.explanation: 4 × 4 = 16 pixels, each with 3 channel values (R, G, B): 16 × 3 = 48.
questions.remediation: Video part 7: Computer Vision; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation: Image processing is a subset of CV; grayscale has one channel; resolution is the number of pixels.
questions.remediation: Video part 7: Computer Vision; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Resolution is the size of the file in MB
Image processing is the superset of Computer Vision
Computer Vision is the superset of image processing
A grayscale image has three channels

questions.question: Rearranging a jumbled sentence into the correct grammatical order is which stage of NLP?
questions.explanation: Syntax deals with the arrangement of words in a grammatically correct order.
questions.remediation: Video part 8: Natural Language Processing; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: For the word 'studies', which is correct?
questions.explanation: Stemming just chops the ending, so the stem may not be a real word; the lemma always is (like flies → fli / fly).
questions.remediation: Video part 8: Natural Language Processing; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: A chatbot that follows pre-written rules, is easy to make and works on a small set of responses is a:
questions.explanation: Script bots work on rules and are easy to make; smart bots need coding and bigger databases.
questions.remediation: Video part 8: Natural Language Processing; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Two documents are lower-cased only (no stop words removed): D1 'The cat sat on the mat', D2 'The dog sat'. How many words are in the dictionary of unique words?
questions.explanation: Unique words: the, cat, sat, on, mat, dog = 6.
questions.remediation: Video part 8: Natural Language Processing; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Using the same dictionary, what is the value for 'the' in the document vector of D1?
questions.explanation: Bag of Words counts frequency: 'the' appears twice in 'the cat sat on the mat'. Word order does not matter.
questions.remediation: Video part 8: Natural Language Processing; then the worksheet practice for this part.
